top_story: Israel’s campaign in southern Lebanon has shifted from intermittent cross-border fire to a broader offensive, with intensified airstrikes on 26 May killing at least 31 people as Israeli forces expanded ground operations under Netanyahu’s pledge to “crush” Hezbollah. This escalation builds on months of attacks that have hit ambulances, hospitals, and rescue workers since early March, deepening civilian vulnerability and eroding the social infrastructure that sustains communities under fire. The Lebanese front is also being shaped by a wider regional crisis after Tehran warned in March that US threats against Iran’s power grid and pressure around the Strait of Hormuz could trigger broader escalation, narrowing space for de-escalation as US-Iran diplomacy stalls. The immediate trajectory points toward a more entrenched multi-front confrontation in which military signaling is increasingly translating into humanitarian collapse.
